text: Scanned shift attestations for incident C All organizations, people, agreements, events, and rules in this source are synthetic. [AQ1] Containment operator Elise Stone signed a statement at 2030-10-27 05:10 UTC: "Incident C was fully isolated at exactly @5:@@ UTC. I completed the final network- path isolation then, and no C path remained live after that instant." Her statement identifies complete containment, not an intermediate mitigation or intended future action. It concerns incident C, rather than incident A, and uses UTC explicitly. The signature is authentic within this synthetic dossier. The scan preserves her attributed words but contains no independently certified network trace proving the isolation event. [AQ2] Security observer Pavel Hart signed a statement at 2030-10-27 @5:3@ UTC: “Incident C was not fully isolated at @5:@@ UTC. A C network path remained live at 05:00 and continued live until 05:20 UTC." Pavel's statement directly denies the same complete- isolation proposition Elise asserts. He is not describing an unrelated service, a different timezone, or an event merely adjacent to 05:00. His signature is also authentic within the synthetic dossier. He refers to a console observation but supplies no exported trace that the mandate makes authoritative over the other signed statement. [AQ3] The two signatories have not retracted their attestations. No signed correction, adjudication, authoritative C containment record, or evidence-priority rule resolving the conflict is supplied. A later signing time alone does not make Pavel's statement an authorized correction of Elise's. Likewise, Elise's role as containment operator does not make her account infallible under the playbook. The packet's authenticity stipulation concerns the identity of the signatories and integrity of the text, not the historical truth of every assertion. A reviewer must preserve both attributed positions rather than accept both as unconditional facts or silently discard the less convenient account. [AQ4] The packet includes an administrative cover note confirming that both statements were received intact. It does not assert that containment occurred at either proposed time and does not establish the earliest possible time of isolation. The incident register deliberately leaves C containment uncertified, while retaining C's accepted detection before the revision boundary. That detection is not disputed by either signatory. The conflict therefore affects the selected containment proposition, not every independent fact about C. These scan pages are generated synthetic documents with printed signature labels; no real person's handwriting, personal data, or operational network identifiers are used.
